name: rAIght
description: Helps process owners build every automation on the lowest step of the automation ladder that does the job, and turn agents that keep repeating themselves into workflows.
scope: Any team that builds its own automations. The sample agents come from HR recruiting, our first pilot
Automations and agents built with external providers: Copilot Studio, Power Automate, OpenAI, n8n
Token use and repeated paths, read from the run logs
Ladder and triage guidance for choosing the step
An inventory of automations with the reason for every agent
Cases an agent could not handle, routed to the process owner
goals: Every automation sits on the lowest step that does the job
Process owners see what their agents really consume
Agents that behave like workflows are found and converted
Token cost and CO₂ stop growing with every new agent

changes: Both dashboards greet you by name and show the one-sentence summary underneath, with the filters on the right.
A new set of icons across the menu, the cards and the Assistant.

The Assistant has a panel for MCP servers and skills. It shows three example servers (Jira, Internal Knowledge Hub, n8n) with a way to connect another one, and three skills you can switch on and off. The servers are a preview: nothing is really connected.
Colours, text, fields, buttons and cards now follow one set of design values, with a lighter top bar and a clearer text font. People are shown with a blue avatar.
Gradients and decorative colours are gone, so the pages look calmer.
A new look: breadcrumbs above each page title, clearer buttons, tags, tables and form fields. It works on small screens too.
Each role has its own home page and menu. The person menu in the top bar switches between process owner, CIO office and Admin.
The CIO office sees a company dashboard with figures per owner. It is read-only and shows no single agent or run.
The Admin gets a Providers page to connect or disconnect providers and an Access page for people and roles. Access moved out of About.
The Start page is gone. The dashboard is the first page.
A floating Assistant on the dashboard answers questions from the sample data. It calls no AI model.
Guidelines are rewritten for colleagues who are not technical: what rAIght does, how it works in three steps, and a short list of words.
New logo mark and favicon, and a deeper blue. Green, red and amber now mean status only.
Plan an automation shows a sketch of the step you picked, with the steps that cost tokens marked.
Plan an automation has a second column with the six steps and starter examples, and shows progress as three rising steps. Guidelines show a sketch of each step next to its description.
You can remove an automation you saved yourself, after a second click to confirm. The sample agents cannot be removed.
Examples, placeholders and hints come from different teams, not only from recruiting.
The Assistant can suggest the ladder step for a task you describe and offer an n8n draft file. It uses rules, not AI, and sends nothing to n8n.
New look with a white sidebar and one blue accent.
The menu follows the work: Dashboard, Plan an automation, Automations and Escalations, with Guidelines and About at the bottom.
Every page has a one-line description under its title.
Escalations show priority tiles and a matrix of cases per agent and category.
Plan an automation is a three-step wizard that saves to Automations.
About has scope, goals and version history, plus a reset for the demo data.
On narrow screens the sidebar collapses into a menu.
App shell with the dashboard, agent detail and the ladder and triage guidelines.
Sample data for five agents, summary figures and training texts.
The clickable demo is published as a static website.
Scope fixed: a clickable demo on sample data with no backend.
The demo script and the design system set the boundary for the build.
